pins.title: Finish before dark
pins.sub: In November the sun sets before 6 pm in Gatlinburg, and it gets dark sooner under the trees. Start early and pick a turnaround time.

pins.title: Quiet trails, open views
pins.sub: Once the leaves drop, ridge views open up and the October crowds thin out. A parking tag is still needed all year.

pins.title: Sunset comes an hour early
pins.sub: The hike that ended in daylight last week now ends in the dark. Start an hour earlier and pack a headlamp anyway.

pins.title: Watch the shady spots
pins.sub: Bridges, boardwalks and shaded rock freeze first and thaw last. The trail can look dry while those stay icy. Slow down and test your footing.

pins.title: Keep it close to you
pins.sub: Cold drains phone batteries fast. Carry it in an inside pocket, download the map before you go and bring a paper backup.

pins.title: Unbuckle first
pins.sub: Open your hip belt and chest strap before you step in, so you can shed the pack if you slip. Fast water above your knees? Turn back.

pins.title: Layers beat one big coat
pins.sub: A heavy coat soaks with sweat on the climb. A fleece over a base layer, with a shell in the pack, lets you adjust as you go.
